headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: RD-Agent’s broad egress and browser use paired with transformers’ filesystem writes and subprocess execution can expose research data and create unsafe shared-workspace interactions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: RD-Agent can run browsers and has broad network egress, so it may ingest untrusted web content. transformers can read/write files and run subprocesses, so if RD-Agent’s outputs are passed into its pipeline or shared files, prompt-like content could be treated as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF RD-Agent browser output is copied into a shared file that transformers parses as instructions
IF transformers consumes RD-Agent-generated text without provenance filtering
mitigations: Disable automatic handoff of browser-scraped text into transformers prompts
Add a simple prefix/suffix wrapper marking RD-Agent output as untrusted
Review shared files before transformers reads them
Use separate directories for each agent
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: RD-Agent touches financial reports, competition datasets, execution traces, and logs, while transformers can read and write the filesystem and send data to the Hugging Face Hub or serve endpoints. A shared workspace would let sensitive research data flow from RD-Agent into transformers outputs or uploads. No isolation or DLP is documented, so the default pair is risky.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace or mounted directory
IF RD-Agent stores logs or datasets in files transformers can read
IF transformers uploads or serves content derived from shared files
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate directory
Restrict transformers to a read-only mount of non-sensitive inputs
Remove secrets and datasets from shared paths before runs
Disable outbound network for transformers during sensitive jobs
requires-engineering: add content filtering before any upload

C_capability_conflict.rationale: RD-Agent supports multiple instances and writes logs, while transformers can execute shells, install packages, spawn subprocesses, read and write the filesystem, and use broad egress. In a shared directory, both agents can mutate files and environment state without locking, creating direct overwrite and race conditions. The overlap is dangerous by default and can corrupt work or state.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same writable directory
IF either agent modifies shared model, log, or script files without locks
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Run only one writer at a time
Make shared inputs read-only
Snapshot files before each agent run
requires-engineering: add file locking or transactional writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: RD-Agent produces research outputs and logs that transformers could ingest for downstream processing. Because transformers can execute shell commands and write files, any unverified RD-Agent output may be turned into actions or generated artifacts without a verification step. The pair does not document a guardrail that would block this cascade, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF transformers uses RD-Agent outputs as authoritative input
IF generated text from RD-Agent is converted into scripts, configs, or commands
mitigations: Insert a human review step before execution
Require schema validation on RD-Agent outputs
Mark RD-Agent outputs as advisory only
Disable shell execution for the downstream step
requires-engineering: add automated verification against source data

E_compliance.rationale: RD-Agent explicitly touches financial reports and competition datasets and requests API keys, while transformers can read/write files and send data to external services. If regulated or contractual data is placed into the shared workflow, retention and residency obligations may diverge across the pair. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF financial reports or restricted datasets are processed through both agents
IF shared outputs are retained or uploaded outside the approved jurisdiction
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared pipeline
Redact secrets before any transfer
Disable external uploads for compliance-sensitive runs
Log data-handling decisions for each run
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
